Its only flaws are that the copy block sits on the yellow circle and the pill text is tiny. B breaks the reading order: SOLSTICE drops below its headline, the Blood Orange pill floats alone at the top centre, and the other two pills are scattered under the CTA with Cucumber Mint jammed against the pink circle's edge. B's left yellow circle is also left as an empty dead zone.

B is a faithful rearrangement with the brand, headline, subhead and pill row grouped on the left and a clear CTA on the right; the pill labels are small. A puts SOLSTICE under the headline, crams the three pills into a cluster on the pink circle away from the copy, and shrinks the CTA into a small button that no longer stands out. A's copy block also sits off-centre with a large empty yellow circle beside it.

B keeps a clean hierarchy and grouping: brand → headline → subhead → pills, with the CTA on the right. A strands the Blood Orange pill at the top centre and separates the other two tiny pills to the bottom right, so the flavour set reads as scattered fragments. A also moves SOLSTICE below the headline and jams the subhead tight under it.
